summary: The Megillah must be read in order and from the scroll, not by heart. It must be read in Hebrew or in a language the listener understands.

chunks.en: If someone reads the Megillah out of order,
chunks.st: With regard to one who reads the Megilla out of order,
chunks.stMore: reading a later section first, and then going back to the earlier section,

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

words.note: He did not do his mitzvah.

chunks.en: If he read it by heart,
chunks.st: If he read it by heart,

chunks.en: or read it in Targum,
chunks.st: or if he read it in Aramaic translation

chunks.en: or in any other language he doesn't understand,
chunks.st: or in any other language that he does not understand,

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: But for people who speak another language, we may read it in their language.
chunks.st: However, for those who speak a foreign language, one may read the Megilla in that foreign language.

words.en: for those who speak another language

chunks.en: And one who speaks another language who heard it in Hebrew has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: And one who speaks a foreign language who heard the Megilla read in Ashurit, i.e., in Hebrew, has fulfilled his obligation.

words.en: and the one who speaks another language

summary: If someone reads the Megillah with breaks or while sleepy, he has done the mitzvah. If he was writing it or checking it, it counts only if he meant to do the mitzvah. A kosher Megillah must be written in Hebrew, on parchment, with ink.

chunks.en: If he read it with breaks,
chunks.st: If one read the Megilla at intervals, pausing and resuming,

chunks.en: or while dozing off, he has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: or while he is dozing off, he has fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If he was writing it,
chunks.st: If one was writing a Megilla,

chunks.en: or explaining it, or fixing mistakes in it,
chunks.explain: And he read every word while doing it.
chunks.st: or expounding upon it, or correcting it,
chunks.stMore: and he read all its words as he was doing so, the following distinction applies:

chunks.en: if he meant to do the mitzvah,
chunks.st: If he had intent to fulfill his obligation with that reading

chunks.en: he has done it. And if not,
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation, but if not,

chunks.en: he has not done it.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If it was written with sam,
chunks.st: If one reads from a Megilla that was written not with ink but with sam

chunks.en: or with sikra, or komos, or kankantom,
chunks.explain: These are kinds of colors, not real ink.
chunks.st: or with sikra or with komos or with kankantom,

chunks.en: or on paper or on diftera,
chunks.explain: Diftera is leather that was not fully made into parchment.
chunks.st: or from a Megilla that was written not on parchment but on neyar or on diftera, a kind of unprocessed leather,

words.note: Leather not fully made into parchment.

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah,
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: unless it is written in Ashuris,
chunks.st: He does not fulfill his obligation unless he reads from a Megilla that is written in Ashurit, i.e., in the Hebrew language and using the Hebrew script,

chunks.en: on parchment and with ink.
chunks.st: upon parchment and with ink.

summary: Someone who travels between a town and a walled city reads on his own day if he plans to go back home. The Rabbis disagree how much of the Megillah one must read to do the mitzvah.

chunks.en: A person from a town who went to a walled city,
chunks.st: With regard to a resident of an unwalled town who went to a walled city,
chunks.stMore: where the Megilla is read on the fifteenth of Adar,

chunks.en: or a person from a walled city who went to a town,
chunks.st: and conversely, a resident of a walled city who went to an unwalled town where it is read on the fourteenth,

chunks.en: if he will go back to his place,
chunks.st: If he is destined to return to his original place,

chunks.en: reads like his own place.
chunks.st: he reads it according to the halakha governing his own place,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not, i.e., if he is not destined to return to his place,

chunks.en: he reads with them.
chunks.explain: With the people of the place where he is now.
chunks.st: he reads with them, the residents of his current location.

chunks.en: And from where must a person read the Megillah
chunks.st: Beginning from where must a person read the Megilla

chunks.en: to do his mitzvah?
chunks.st: in order to fulfill his obligation?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: All of it. Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: He must read all of it. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: From "There was a Jewish man."
chunks.explain: That is where Mordechai is first told about.
chunks.st: He need read only from “There was a certain Jew” (Esther 2:5).

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: From "After these things."
chunks.explain: That is where Haman is first told about.
chunks.st: From “After these things” (Esther 3:1).

summary: Everyone may read the Megillah except a deaf person, a person who isn't thinking clearly, and a child. Some mitzvos are done only after sunrise, but if they were done from dawn, they count.

chunks.en: Everyone may read the Megillah,
chunks.st: Everyone is fit to read the Megilla,

chunks.en: except a deaf person,
chunks.st: except for a deaf person,

chunks.en: a person who isn't thinking clearly, and a child.
chunks.st: an imbecile, and a minor.

words.note: A person whose mind does not work clearly.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says a child may read it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda disagrees and says that a minor is fit to read the Megilla.

chunks.en: We do not read the Megillah,
chunks.st: One may not read the Megilla,

chunks.en: and we do not do a bris milah,
chunks.st: nor perform a circumcision,

chunks.en: and we do not go to the mikveh,
chunks.st: nor immerse himself in a ritual bath,

chunks.en: and we do not sprinkle the purifying water,
chunks.explain: Special water was sprinkled to make people tahor.
chunks.st: nor sprinkle water of purification to purify people and objects that had contracted ritual impurity through contact with a corpse until after sunrise.

chunks.en: And also a woman who is waiting one day to become tahor
chunks.st: And also a woman who observes a clean day for each day she experiences a discharge, i.e., a woman who experienced one or two days of non-menstrual bleeding, and must now wait until a day has passed without any discharge of blood before regaining ritual purity,

words.note: Together: one clean day to make up for one day of tumah.

chunks.en: may not go to the mikveh
chunks.st: she too may not immerse herself

words.en: she may go to the mikveh

chunks.en: until the sun comes up.
chunks.st: until the sun has risen.

chunks.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִשֶּׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר, כָּשֵׁר:
chunks.en: And for all of them, if they did it from dawn, it counts.
chunks.explain: Dawn is when the first light shows, before the sun comes up.
chunks.st: And with regard to all these activities that are supposed to be performed during the day, if one did them after daybreak, i.e., after the appearance of the first light of the sun, even before sunrise, they are valid, as at this point it is already considered daytime.

summary: Many mitzvos that are done by day may be done any time during the whole day, like reading the Megillah, Hallel, shofar and lulav, and many of the jobs of the korbanos.

chunks.en: The whole day is fine for reading the Megillah,
chunks.st: Although it is preferable to fulfill a particular day’s mitzva at the earliest possible hour, the entire day is a valid time for reading the Megilla;

chunks.en: for saying Hallel,
chunks.st: for reciting hallel;

chunks.en: for blowing the shofar,
chunks.st: for sounding the shofar on Rosh HaShana;

chunks.en: for taking the lulav,
chunks.st: for taking the lulav and the other species on Sukkot;

chunks.en: for davening Mussaf,
chunks.st: for the additional prayer recited on Shabbat and other occasions;

chunks.en: for the Mussaf korbanos, for the confession over the bulls,
chunks.explain: Bulls brought for a mistake of the Sanhedrin or the Kohen Gadol.
chunks.st: and for the additional offerings sacrificed in the Temple on these occasions. And the entire day is also a valid time for the confession over the bulls
chunks.stMore: brought by the Sanhedrin or by the High Priest to atone for mistakes they had made in their instruction to the people;

chunks.en: for the declaration about maaser,
chunks.explain: Saying that all the maaser was given properly.
chunks.st: for the declaration made on the last day of Passover in the fourth and seventh year of the Sabbatical cycle, stating that one’s obligations with regard to tithes

chunks.en: for the confession of Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: and for the confession of sins made by the High Priest on Yom Kippur
chunks.stMore: over the special offerings brought on that day.

chunks.en: for leaning hands on a korban, for shechting it,
chunks.st: The entire day is also a valid time for placing hands on the head of an offering; for slaughtering an offering;

words.note: Leaning hands on the head of a korban.

chunks.en: for waving it, for bringing it close to the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: for waving those offerings that require waving in the Temple; for bringing meal-offerings near to the altar;

chunks.en: for taking a handful of flour and for burning it,
chunks.st: for scooping out a fistful of flour from a meal-offering in order to burn it on the altar; and for burning the fistful of flour on the altar;

chunks.en: for melikah, and for catching the blood,
chunks.explain: Melikah is how the Kohen shechted a bird korban.
chunks.st: for pinching the necks of the turtledoves and young pigeons sacrificed as offerings in the Temple; and for receiving the blood of an offering in a vessel;

chunks.en: for sprinkling, and for giving the sotah to drink,
chunks.explain: The sotah drank special water in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: and for sprinkling blood on the altar and on the curtain separating between the Holy and the Holy of Holies. And the entire day is also a valid time for giving a woman suspected by her husband of having been unfaithful [sota] to drink

words.note: A wife who had to drink special water in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: for the eglah arufah,
chunks.explain: A calf brought when a person was found dead and no one knew what happened.
chunks.st: for breaking the neck of the heifer
chunks.stMore: as part of the procedure followed when a corpse is found outside a town and it is not known who caused his death (see Deuteronomy 21:1–9);

words.en: and for the breaking of the neck of

chunks.en: and for making the metzora tahor.
chunks.st: and for all the steps in the purification process of the leper (see Leviticus 14:1–20).

summary: Mitzvos done at night may be done all night long. The rule: a daytime mitzvah may be done all day, and a nighttime mitzvah all night.
stIntro: Correspondingly, all the mitzvot that must be performed at night may be performed anytime during the night:

chunks.en: The whole night is fine
chunks.st: The entire night is a valid time for

chunks.en: for cutting the omer,
chunks.explain: The omer was barley cut on the night after the first day of Pesach.
chunks.st: reaping the omer of barley on the night following the first day of Passover,

chunks.en: and for burning the fats and the limbs of korbanos.
chunks.st: for burning the fats of offerings that had been brought during the preceding day, and for burning the limbs of burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Something whose mitzvah is by day
chunks.st: Something that it is a mitzva to perform during the day

chunks.en: is fine all day.
chunks.st: is valid if performed anytime during the entire day;

chunks.en: Something whose mitzvah is at night
chunks.st: something that it is a mitzva to perform at night

chunks.en: is fine all night.
chunks.st: is valid if performed anytime during the entire night.
